title: Feature flag rollout per account/deployment for autoscaling bounds + predictive mode
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
body:
Context
Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) and predictive mode are behavior-changing and must be gated for safe rollout and fast rollback. We need per-account (and ideally per-deployment) enablement with safe defaults, deterministic evaluation, and an ops-friendly kill switch.

Goal
Implement gating and rollout controls so that:
1) Existing Dedicated customers see no behavior change until explicitly enabled.
2) We can enable bounds and predictive mode for select pilot accounts/deployments.
3) We can disable (rollback) predictive mode quickly if it causes oscillation/latency regressions.
4) Flag evaluation is deterministic and auditable (what was enabled at decision time).

Scope
- Define flags (names, scope, defaults)
- Add flag evaluation in the autoscaler decision loop and control plane policy evaluation
- Add safe rollback mechanisms (global kill switch + per-account disable)
- Add observability + logging for effective flag state
- Add admin/operator tooling and runbook notes (minimal for pilot)

Non-goals
- Customer-facing self-serve enablement (Console UX is covered elsewhere)
- Complex percentage rollouts across all tenants (nice-to-have; start with explicit allowlists)

Proposed flags
A) dedicated.autoscaling_bounds.enabled
- Scope: account_id, optional deployment_id override
- Default: false
- Effect: when false, autoscaler ignores min/max bounds fields (treat as unset) and preserves current platform-driven scaling.

B) dedicated.predictive_autoscaling.enabled
- Scope: account_id, optional deployment_id override
- Default: false
- Effect: when false, autoscaler does not consume forecast inputs; reactive scaling only.

C) dedicated.predictive_autoscaling.kill_switch
- Scope: global
- Default: false
- Effect: when true, predictive mode is forced off regardless of per-account enablement. Used for incident response.

D) dedicated.scaling_policy_api.write_enabled (optional for pilot)
- Scope: account_id
- Default: false
- Effect: when false, updates to scaling policy fields are rejected (or accepted but stored as inert) depending on control plane approach. See notes below.

Semantics / precedence (important)
- Kill switch (C) wins over everything.
- For predictive mode:
  - Predictive is enabled only if (B == true) AND (C == false) AND deployment has predictive_mode configured.
- For bounds:
  - Bounds enforcement is enabled only if (A == true) AND deployment has min/max set.
- Backward compatibility: if flags are false, existing deployments that already have bounds fields (from migrations/backfill) must continue behaving exactly as before; the fields are inert.

Implementation plan
1) Flag source
- Use Control Plane feature gate service (FeatureGate) as the single source of truth.
- Provide evaluation by account_id and optional deployment_id.
- Autoscaler will fetch a signed/effective gate snapshot for each deployment on a TTL (60s) to avoid hot-path network dependency.

2) Data model / API
- Add "effective_gates" to the autoscaler decision context (not persisted long-term).
- Include a "gate_snapshot_id" (hash) in scaling decision audit events so we can correlate incidents to the flag state.

3) Caching + consistency
- Autoscaler caches flags with:
  - TTL: 60s
  - jitter: +/- 10s to avoid herd refresh
  - hard max age: 5m (after which fail closed to defaults; see Failure modes)
- Control plane caches can be longer (5m) but must reflect global kill switch within 60s.

4) Failure modes / safe defaults
- If the feature gate service is unavailable:
  - Treat gates as disabled (fail closed) for both bounds and predictive mode.
  - Exception: if bounds were already actively enforced for a deployment and the gate snapshot cannot be refreshed, continue using the last known gate state for up to 5m to avoid flapping; after 5m, log error and fail closed to disabled (reverting to current behavior). (This is a tradeoff; see Risks.)
- If the kill switch value cannot be fetched, assume kill switch is ON (predictive disabled) but keep bounds gating based on last known state (since bounds are a safety guardrail rather than a risk factor).

5) Rollback mechanisms
- Global kill switch to disable predictive mode within ~1 minute.
- Per-account disable for both bounds and predictive.
- Support tool: internal admin CLI command to print effective flags for account/deployment and last refresh time.

6) Observability
Metrics:
- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_refresh_success_total{region}
- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_refresh_failure_total{region,reason}
- dedicated_autoscaler_gate_snapshot_age_seconds{region}
- dedicated_autoscaler_effective_predictive_enabled{account_id,deployment_id,region} (sampled; watch cardinality)
- dedicated_autoscaler_effective_bounds_enabled{account_id,deployment_id,region} (sampled)
Logs:
- Structured log on gate refresh with snapshot_id, scopes matched, cache age.
Audit:
- Scaling decision events include: effective_bounds_enabled, effective_predictive_enabled, kill_switch_state, snapshot_id.

7) Testing
- Unit tests:
  - precedence ordering (kill switch overrides)
  - fail closed behavior when gate service errors
  - per-deployment override takes precedence over account flag
- Integration tests:
  - autoscaler loop consumes gates and produces correct bounded_desired behavior only when enabled
  - kill switch disables predictive even if policy asks for predictive

Acceptance criteria
- Default OFF for all accounts.
- Can enable bounds and predictive independently per account.
- Can override on/off per deployment within an account.
- Global kill switch disables predictive within <= 60s.
- Gate evaluation results are visible in logs and included in scaling decision audit events.
- Failure to fetch gates does not cause crashes; behavior is deterministic and fails closed.

Risks / open questions
- Fail-closed after last-known state expiry could create a sudden behavior change mid-incident (e.g., predictive suddenly disables). Mitigation: keep kill switch explicit for predictive; consider extending last-known for bounds indefinitely since bounds are protective. Need SRE signoff.
- Cardinality: per-deployment labels can explode. For effective_enabled metrics, we should sample and/or aggregate by account tier; keep detailed per-deployment in logs only.
- Control plane write gating (flag D): prefer accepting and storing policy fields even when disabled (so pilot can pre-configure), but ensure UI communicates "not active". Product/Console alignment required.

References / related work
- Epic: PM-1842
- Ticket: ENG-22146 (scaling decision audit events)
- Ticket: ENG-22142 (predictive signal ingestion)
- GitHub: PR-48263 (account/deployment-scoped feature flags + safe rollbacks)

Rollout plan (pilot)
- Week 1: enable bounds for 1 internal test account + 1 pilot account in us-east.
- Week 2: enable predictive for the same pilot account with kill switch on standby; monitor oscillation/latency.
- Expand to 3 pilot accounts if metrics stable.

Done definition
- Flags implemented, defaults set to OFF.
- Kill switch implemented and verified in canary.
- Runbook snippet added to dedicated autoscaler troubleshooting (how to verify/flip gates).
- Alerts added for gate refresh failures (non-paging during pilot; paging only if combined with scaling SLO violations).
